newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Police sources said the head of the provisional legislature, Rita Fan, got threatening calls last week demanding she not attend the swearing in of the interim council, but she denied receiving any such calls or letters.
-- Three trainee firemen were overcome by intense head in a smode-filled room during a training exercise.
-- MING PAO -- The decision by the Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp to increase fares despite a huge profit last year has caused public anger.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- London revealed that Britain only has oral agreements with 80 countries over granting Hong Kong BNO passport holders visa-free entry. But the British consulate in Hong Kong said these oral agreements should remain effective.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa met Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs Commissioner in Hong Kong Ma Yuzhen. They stressed mutual respect and cooperation, and believed the government and the commission would establish a smooth working relationship.

-- TAI KUNG PAO --Recent suveys showed over half of Chinese wanted to buy their own apartments instead of staying in government housing. In Beijing, 64 percent of residents placed owning a private car ahead of buying a nice aprtment.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Sources said China would investigate unlawful behaviour by some red-chip companies in Hong Kong, But the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission refused to comment.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- Seven Hong Kong BNO passport holders were stranded in Combodia and had gone to the British and Chinese consulates for help. China's Foreign Affairs Commission said Chinese consulates had the responsibility to give BNO passport holders assistance.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Sources said the Hong Kong Futures Exchanges would launch red-chip index futures in two months in the latest move to provide investors with hedging tools in the highly-volatile sector.
-- A Goldman Sachs report suggested that red-chip stocks must deliver assets injections worth at least HK$580 billion in the next 18 months to stave off investor disappointment.

-- HONG KONG STANDARD -- An urgent Court of Appeal hearing was set after government lawyers took the "exceptional" step of pressing for a direct referral to the highest available court to "settle once and for all" legality of the Provisional Legislative Council.
